text: Declare a project's developer-environment dependencies in a Brewfile committed to the repo, like package.json or Gemfile
quote: Adding a `Brewfile` to a project's repository (like you might a `package.json`, `Gemfile` or `requirements.txt`) is a nicer way of encoding project dependencies for developer environments.

text: Describe the desired end state in a Brewfile instead of listing the brew commands to run
quote: Rather than specifying the `brew` commands you wish to run, you can specify the state you wish to reach.

text: Run a single command to install all of a project's dependencies and start its services
quote: It allows you to tell users to run a single command to install all dependencies for a project and start any services.

text: brew bundle dump writes the currently installed formulae, casks, taps and other package types to a Brewfile
quote: `brew bundle dump` is Homebrew's installed-state snapshot command: it records supported installed formulae, casks, taps and other package types as a `Brewfile`.

text: brew bundle manages casks, Mac App Store apps, VS Code extensions, Go, Cargo, npm, uv, Flatpak, WinGet and Krew dependencies
quote: Bundler for non-Ruby dependencies from Homebrew formulae, Homebrew casks, Mac App Store dependencies, VSCode (and forks/variants) extensions, Go packages, Cargo packages, uv tools, Flatpak packages, WinGet packages, Krew plugins and npm pac

text: brew bundle check reports whether an install would change anything, so scripts can run check || install
quote: You can use this behaviour in scripts like so: brew bundle check || brew bundle install

text: Set up project dependencies with one command in CI services such as GitHub Actions
quote: one command can set up project dependencies across these environments and in continuous-integration services such as GitHub Actions.

text: Run a shell inside a brew bundle exec environment
quote: Run your shell in a `brew bundle exec` environment.

text: Generate a new formula or cask definition from a source URL with brew create
quote:
$ brew create https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ffmpeg-8.1.1.tar.xz
Created .../homebrew-core/Formula/ffmpeg.rb

text: brew tap adds third-party repositories that provide formulae, casks and external commands
quote: The `brew tap` command adds repositories that Homebrew can use for formulae, casks and external commands.

text: Taps can come from GitHub or from any URL that Git supports
quote: The one-argument form assumes a repository on GitHub, while the two-argument form accepts any URL supported by Git.

text: brew untap removes taps, deletes their local repositories and stops loading their contents
quote: brew untap <user>/<repository> [...] removes one or more taps. Homebrew deletes the local repositories and no longer loads their contents.

text: brew tap --repair restores missing tap manpage and shell-completion symlinks
quote: `brew tap --repair` adds missing tap manpage and shell-completion symlinks.

text: Select a formula from a specific tap by using its fully qualified name
quote: Use the fully qualified name to select the formula from a particular tap

text: Tapping a repo does not grant whole-tap trust; installing a fully qualified item trusts only that item
quote: Tapping a repository does not grant whole-tap trust. Install a fully qualified item to trust only that item

text: brew install no longer needs sudo after Homebrew's initial installation
quote: you don't need _sudo_ after Homebrew's initial installation when you `brew install`

text: Homebrew can be installed for a non-admin account
quote: Homebrew can be installed for a non-admin account.

text: Disable all of Homebrew's sudo calls with HOMEBREW_NO_SUDO=1
quote: To disable Homebrew's sudo calls explicitly: export HOMEBREW_NO_SUDO=1

text: Install software not packaged for your Linux distribution without sudo
quote: It can also install software not packaged for your Linux distribution without requiring `sudo`.

text: Install up-to-date software versions on hosts with an old Linux distribution
quote: Install up-to-date versions of software when your host distribution is old

text: Use the same package manager across macOS, Linux and Windows
quote: Use the same package manager to manage your macOS, Linux and Windows systems

text: Automatically uninstall formulae that were only installed as dependencies and are no longer needed
quote: Uninstall formulae that were only installed as a dependency of another formula and are now no longer needed.

text: Prebuilt bottles matching your system are downloaded and installed automatically by brew install
quote: When the formula being installed defines a bottle matching your system, it will be downloaded and installed automatically when you run `brew install <formula>`.

text: Build a formula from source on request with --build-from-source
quote: the user requests it (by specifying `--build-from-source`)

text: Generate bottle files and bottle DSL so taps can provide their own bottles or support a non-default Cellar
quote: This generates a bottle file in the current directory and outputs the bottle DSL for insertion into the formula file.

text: Install a bottle for another architecture with --bottle-arch when the formula requires it
quote: Use `--bottle-arch=` only when the formula intentionally requires another architecture and its compatibility has been reviewed.

text: Installs each package into its own keg in the Cellar and symlinks its files into the prefix
quote: It installs each package into its own keg inside the Cellar, then symlinks its files into the prefix

text: Casks install upstream prebuilt binaries such as applications, fonts and plugins
quote: Casks are package definitions that install upstream pre-built binaries such as applications, fonts and plugins.

text: Install compatible app casks to a writable destination with --appdir
quote: For compatible app casks, use a writable destination such as `brew install --cask --appdir="$HOME/Applications" <cask>`.

text: brew upgrade --greedy also upgrades casks that auto-update outside Homebrew
quote: Some casks auto-update outside Homebrew, so use `brew upgrade --greedy` if you want Homebrew to update them too.

text: Turn off Homebrew's anonymous aggregate analytics
quote:
`brew analytics off`

Turn Homebrew’s analytics off.

text: Anonymised install, build and OS usage data is publicly viewable at formulae.brew.sh/analytics
quote: View anonymised install, build and operating system usage data at formulae.brew.sh/analytics.

text: Run brew as root from MDM, Munki or Jamf while operations execute as the logged-in console user
quote: This is intended for MDM, Munki and Jamf workflows where `brew` is invoked as root but Homebrew operations should run as the logged-in console user.

text: Manage an existing installation from administrative scripts and scheduled jobs, even when no user is logged in
quote: Use this in administrative scripts and scheduled jobs to manage an existing installation, including when no user is logged in.

text: macOS .pkg installer supports interactive or unattended MDM installs
quote: If you're on macOS, try our `.pkg` installer for interactive or unattended MDM installs.

text: Set an alternate install user for .pkg installs done at the login window
quote: To specify an alternate install user, such as when the package is installed at the login window before a user has logged in, create /var/tmp/.homebrew_pkg_user.plist

text: Run the installation script non-interactively by setting NONINTERACTIVE=1
quote: prepend `NONINTERACTIVE=1` to the installation command

text: The install script explains what it will do and pauses before doing it
quote: Paste that in the macOS Terminal, a Linux shell or WSL. The script explains what it will do and then pauses before it does it.

text: Search formula names and cask tokens by substring or regular expression
quote: Perform a substring search of cask tokens and formula names for text. If text is flanked by slashes, it is interpreted as a regular expression.

text: Edit command aliases in a text editor, one at a time or all at once
quote: Edit aliases in a text editor. Either one or all aliases may be opened at once.

text: List brew info --json output for all current homebrew-core formulae or homebrew-cask casks
quote: List the `brew info --json` output for all current Homebrew/homebrew-core formulae or Homebrew/homebrew-cask casks.

text: Run a strict audit on a package definition with brew audit --strict
quote: perform a strict audit on a package you use e.g. `brew audit --strict ffmpeg` for FFmpeg
